newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BNDES says no new CVRD bid specs needed.
newsitem.headline: BNDES says no new CVRD bid specs needed.

text.p: Brazil's government may reschedule the privatization auction of state miner Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) as many times as it needs without publishing new tender documents, a top BNDES official said.

Jose Pio Borges, vice-president of Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) and privatization chief, told reporters that the law only requires new tender details if there are changes in the rules for the sell-off, including base price or payment rules.
"As we understand that there are no changes (of that nature), there is no need to publish new tender documents," he said.

Pio Borges's comments came to clarify newspaper reports saying that the government would be able to reset the auction, which has been rescheduled three times already, only during a certain period of time, possibly 10 days.
After that period, the BNDES would have to publish new tender details which would delay the auction even further, the papers said.

Pio Borges also said 23 injunctions had been granted by different judges, of which 19 were revoked. The government still has to overturn four injunctions, one granted in a Rio court and three in Sao Paulo courts.
The chairman of Brazilian steel maker CSN, which is leading one of the two consortia bidding for CVRD, said he thought the sale would take place next week, probably Tuesday.

"The nucleus of our consortium has been created. It will continue in its present form independently of whether the auction takes place next week or not," Benjamin Steinbruch told reporters at a separate press conference.
He said the costs incurred by the delay in the auction were "uncomfortable," but they would not discourage the consortium from continuing in its bid.
These costs, he explained, were not related to financial guarantees, but to any financing consortia may have agreed with banks.
The CSN-led consortium contains four local pension funds, NationsBank Corp and Opportunity Asset Management, an offshore investment fund.
Steinbruch added the consortium had signed a letter of intent with South African mining company Gencor, in which Gencor agreed to join the consortium, should it win the auction.

The second consortium competing in the auction is being led by Brazilian metal, cement and pulp group Votorantim in conjunction with South Africa's Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd ((-- Fatima Cristina, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
